newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end slightly up, thin volumes.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end slightly up, thin volumes.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished flat to slightly higher Wednesday after early gains led to subsequent profit-taking amid thin activity.

"Basically prices rose strongly early, especially in London, and that was followed by declines amid profit-taking," said a trader at a large Argentine bank. Still, even if the market once again failed to break important resistance levels, the expectation is that it will firm, said the trader.
Argentina's FRB due 2005 was flat at 83-3/8, while the local dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose 0.10 to 119.80.
"The market's tendency continues to be higher, for bonds as well as stocks, but since Clinton's re-election was discounted, it was normal to expect profit-taking today," said an analyst.
The trader said "this session's trading volumes were insignificant," testifying to the fact that there were still few investors active in the market.
But "I don't see any clouds on the horizon for the market - if there are more losses I would use it as a buying opportunity," added the trader.
In the money markets, call money rates rose to 6.88 percent from 6.85 percent.
